Interesting. Off the top of my head I could only suggest making sure you have whatever driver is necessary for that bridge, but I'm almost positive it would already be set up. Apart from that, and I know this is obvious but just in case, those enclosures for desktop hard drives can't be powered by a usb port alone. Is there an external power adapter that's plugged in securely and everything? And any power button on the enclosure itself is on? And you are sure you have the drive installed in the enclosure properly with a sata cable and power cable? And you can hear it spin up when you turn it on and everything?

You might also try it in a Windows machine if you have one available. In addition to verifying that it works, make sure it is removed properly as suggested before. Linux is pretty good about fixing unproperly mounted ntfs drives these days but it doesn't hurt to check everything.

You could also try booting from a live cd/dvd/flash disk with something like Ubuntu or Mint and see if those distros recognize your drive out of the box.
